summary: The main article describes a Cp*Co(III)-catalyzed synthesis of isoquinolines via site-selective C-H activation. It includes optimization tables comparing cobalt and rhodium catalysts, scope tables for various oximes and alkynes, and mechanistic schemes including deuterium labeling and proposed pathways.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Scheme 1. Cp*Rh III - and Cp*Co III -catalyzed isoquinoline synthesis; site selectivity with unsymmetrical oxime derivatives and alkynes.
items.description: This scheme compares the general reaction of O-acyloximes with alkynes using Rh(III) versus Co(III) catalysts, highlighting the site-selectivity challenges.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Table 1. Optimization studies and control experiments.
items.description: This table details the screening of catalysts, silver salts, bases, and temperatures to optimize the yield and selectivity of the isoquinoline synthesis.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Table 2. Scope of unsymmetrical O-acyloximes 1.
items.description: This table explores the substrate scope of various meta-substituted O-acyloximes reacting with terminal and internal alkynes.

items.heading: Table 3
items.caption: Table 3. Scope of terminal alkynes 2.
items.description: This table demonstrates the compatibility of different terminal alkynes (aryl, alkyl, heteroaryl) with symmetrical O-acyloximes.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scheme 2. H/D exchange experiments under (a) Cp*Co III catalysis and (b) Cp*Rh III catalysis.
items.description: This scheme shows deuterium labeling results that confirm the superior site-selectivity of the cobalt catalyst over the rhodium catalyst.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Figure 1. Possible reaction pathways to form isoquinolines under Cp*Co III catalysis
items.description: This figure illustrates four potential mechanistic pathways (a-d) for the cobalt-catalyzed annulation reaction.
